events.title: Lynx 2.0 — text-only web browser
events.summary: Lynx 2.0 shipped in March 1992 as a terminal-based browser for Unix and VMS — the main way many universities accessed the early web without graphics.
events.about: Lynx rendered pages as plain text in a terminal: links listed by number, no images, no JavaScript. It stayed essential on slow connections, blind-accessible browsing, and server-side automation for decades — and still runs today for scripting and accessibility testing.

narrative.whyChosen: Lynx proved the web was not only a graphical desktop phenomenon.
narrative.whyImportant: It made the web usable on text terminals and influenced accessibility and command-line tooling for the open web.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers and students on Unix shells had no practical graphical browser — they needed a fast, keyboard-driven way to read linked documents.
